sanskrit: trātāraṃ nādhyagacchanta gāvaḥ paṅkagatā iva pipīlikā iva kṣuṇṇā durbalā balinā raṇe
english: They could find no deliverer, like cattle mired in the mud, like ants trampled underfoot — the weak crushed by the strong in battle.

sanskrit: mahārathaṃ bhārata duṣpradharṣaṃ; śaraughiṇaṃ pratapantaṃ narendrān bhīṣmaṃ na śekuḥ prativīkṣituṃ te; śarārciṣaṃ sūryam ivātapantam
english: O Bhārata, upon that mighty car-warrior, unassailable, pouring forth floods of arrows and scorching the kings, upon Bhīṣma they could not so much as look — blazing with shafts for rays like the burning sun.

sanskrit: vimṛdnatas tasya tu pāṇḍusenām; astaṃ jagāmātha sahasraraśmiḥ tato balānāṃ śramakarśitānāṃ; mano 'vahāraṃ prati saṃbabhūva
english: As he ground down the host of the Pāṇḍavas, the thousand-rayed one went to his setting; then in the armies, worn out by toil, the mind turned toward withdrawal.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yudhyatām eva teṣāṃ tu bhāskare 'stam upāgate saṃdhyā samabhavad ghorā nāpaśyāma tato raṇam
english: Saṃjaya said: While they were still fighting, when the sun had reached its setting, a dreadful twilight came on, and we could no longer see the battle.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā saṃdhyāṃ saṃdṛśya bhārata vadhyamānaṃ balaṃ cāpi bhīṣmeṇāmitraghātinā
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, O Bhārata, beholding the twilight and his host being slaughtered by Bhīṣma, slayer of foes,

sanskrit: muktaśastraṃ parāvṛttaṃ palāyanaparāyaṇam bhīṣmaṃ ca yudhi saṃrabdham anuyāntaṃ mahārathān
english: its weapons let fall, turned about and bent on flight, and Bhīṣma raging in the fight, pursuing the mighty car-warriors —

sanskrit: somakāṃś ca jitān dṛṣṭvā nirutsāhān mahārathān cintayitvā ciraṃ dhyātvā avahāram arocayat
english: and seeing the Somakas vanquished and the great car-warriors dispirited, having pondered long and reflected, he resolved upon a withdrawal.

sanskrit: tato 'vahāraṃ sainyānāṃ cakre rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tathaiva tava sainyānām avahāro hy abhūt tadā
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira ordered the withdrawal of his troops; and in like manner there was a withdrawal of your troops as well at that time.

sanskrit: tato 'vahāraṃ sainyānāṃ kṛtvā tatra mahārathāḥ nyaviśanta kuruśreṣṭha saṃgrāme kṣatavikṣatāḥ
english: Then, having drawn back the troops, the great car-warriors there encamped, O best of the Kurus, hacked and wounded in the fray.

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya samare karma cintayānās tu pāṇḍavāḥ nālabhanta tadā śāntiṃ bhṛśaṃ bhīṣmeṇa pīḍitāḥ
english: But the Pāṇḍavas, brooding on Bhīṣma's deeds in the battle, could find no peace then, sorely harried by Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo 'pi samare jitvā pāṇḍavān saha sṛñjayaiḥ pūjyamānas tava sutair vandyamānaś ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma too, having conquered in battle the Pāṇḍavas together with the Sṛñjayas, honored by your sons and extolled, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: nyaviśat kurubhiḥ sārdhaṃ hṛṣṭarūpaiḥ samantataḥ tato rātriḥ samabhavat sarvabhūtapramohinī
english: encamped together with the Kurus, who were joyful on every side; then came the night, that bewilders all living beings.

sanskrit: tasmin rātrimukhe ghore pāṇḍavā vṛṣṇibhiḥ saha sṛñjayāś ca durādharṣā mantrāya samupāviśan
english: In that dread nightfall the Pāṇḍavas, together with the Vṛṣṇis and the unassailable Sṛñjayas, sat down to take counsel.

sanskrit: ātmaniḥśreyasaṃ sarve prāptakālaṃ mahābalāḥ mantrayām āsur avyagrā mantraniścayakovidāḥ
english: All those mighty ones, skilled in resolving deliberations, took counsel, unperturbed, upon what would be best for them and fitting to the hour.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā mantrayitvā ciraṃ nṛpa vāsudevaṃ samudvīkṣya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, having deliberated long, O king, looked up at Vāsudeva and spoke these words:

sanskrit: paśya kṛṣṇa mahātmānaṃ bhīṣmaṃ bhīmaparākramam gajaṃ nalavanānīva vimṛdnantaṃ balaṃ mama
english: "Behold, Kṛṣṇa, the great-souled Bhīṣma of terrible prowess, crushing my host as an elephant crushes thickets of reeds.

sanskrit: na caivainaṃ mahātmānam utsahāmo nirīkṣitum lelihyamānaṃ sainyeṣu pravṛddham iva pāvakam
english: We dare not even look upon that great-souled one, who licks among the armies like a fire grown high.

sanskrit: yathā ghoro mahānāgas takṣako vai viṣolbaṇaḥ tathā bhīṣmo raṇe kṛṣṇa tīkṣṇaśastraḥ pratāpavān
english: As the dread great serpent Takṣaka, swollen with venom, so is Bhīṣma in battle, O Kṛṣṇa — sharp-weaponed and full of fiery might.

sanskrit: gṛhītacāpaḥ samare vimuñcaṃś ca śitāñ śarān śakyo jetuṃ yamaḥ kruddho vajrapāṇiś ca devarāṭ
english: With bow in hand in battle, loosing his whetted shafts — Yama enraged might be conquered, and the thunderbolt-wielding king of the gods,

sanskrit: varuṇaḥ pāśabhṛd vāpi sagado vā dhaneśvaraḥ na tu bhīṣmaḥ susaṃkruddhaḥ śakyo jetuṃ mahāhave
english: or Varuṇa bearing his noose, or the lord of wealth with his mace — but Bhīṣma in his fury cannot be conquered in great battle.

sanskrit: so 'ham evaṃ gate kṛṣṇa nimagnaḥ śokasāgare ātmano buddhidaurbalyād bhīṣmam āsādya saṃyuge
english: So am I, things having come to this pass, O Kṛṣṇa, sunk in an ocean of grief, having encountered Bhīṣma in the fight through my own weakness of judgment.

sanskrit: vanaṃ yāsyāmi durdharṣa śreyo me tatra vai gatam na yuddhaṃ rocaye kṛṣṇa hanti bhīṣmo hi naḥ sadā
english: I shall go to the forest, O unassailable one — there indeed lies my welfare. I take no joy in this war, Kṛṣṇa, for Bhīṣma slays us without ceasing.

sanskrit: yathā prajvalitaṃ vahniṃ pataṃgaḥ samabhidravan ekato mṛtyum abhyeti tathāhaṃ bhīṣmam īyivān
english: As a moth rushing upon a blazing fire goes straight to its death, so have I come against Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: kṣayaṃ nīto 'smi vārṣṇeya rājyahetoḥ parākramī bhrātaraś caiva me śūrāḥ sāyakair bhṛśapīḍitāḥ
english: I am brought to ruin, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, valiant though I am, for the sake of a kingdom; and my heroic brothers are sorely tormented by his shafts.

sanskrit: matkṛte bhrātṛsauhārdād rājyāt prabhraṃśanaṃ gatāḥ parikliṣṭā tathā kṛṣṇā matkṛte madhusūdana
english: For my sake, out of brotherly love, they have been cast down from the kingdom; and Kṛṣṇā too has been brought to grief for my sake, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ bahu manye 'haṃ jīvitaṃ hy adya durlabham jīvitasyādya śeṣeṇa cariṣye dharmam uttamam
english: Life I hold dear, for life today is hard to keep; with the remnant of life that is left me this day I will follow the highest dharma.

sanskrit: yadi te 'ham anugrāhyo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha keśava svadharmasyāvirodhena tad udāhara keśava
english: If I, together with my brothers, am worthy of your grace, O Keśava, then declare it to me, Keśava, in a manner not at odds with my own dharma."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vacas tasya kāruṇyād bahuvistaram pratyuvāca tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sāntvayāno yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Hearing this his speech, uttered at length out of compassion, Kṛṣṇa then replied, comforting Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: dharmaputra viṣādaṃ tvaṃ mā kṛthāḥ satyasaṃgara yasya te bhrātaraḥ śūrā durjayāḥ śatrusūdanāḥ
english: "Son of Dharma, true to your covenant, do not give way to despair — you whose brothers are heroes, hard to vanquish, slayers of foes:

sanskrit: arjuno bhīmasenaś ca vāyvagnisamatejasau mādrīputrau ca vikrāntau tridaśānām iveśvarau
english: Arjuna and Bhīmasena, equal in splendor to Wind and Fire, and the two valiant sons of Mādrī, like lords among the gods.

sanskrit: māṃ vā niyuṅkṣva sauhārdād yotsye bhīṣmeṇa pāṇḍava tvatprayukto hy ahaṃ rājan kiṃ na kuryāṃ mahāhave
english: Or set me to the task, out of our friendship, O Pāṇḍava, and I will fight with Bhīṣma; for, charged by you, O king, what would I not do in the great battle?

sanskrit: haniṣyāmi raṇe bhīṣmam āhūya puruṣarṣabham paśyatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ yadi necchati phalgunaḥ
english: I will challenge and slay in battle that bull among men, Bhīṣma, before the very eyes of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons — if Phalguna is unwilling.

sanskrit: yadi bhīṣme hate rājañ jayaṃ paśyasi pāṇḍava hantāsmy ekarathenādya kuruvṛddhaṃ pitāmaham
english: If, O king, you see victory in Bhīṣma's death, O Pāṇḍava, I will this day, with a single car, slay the aged grandsire of the Kurus.

sanskrit: paśya me vikramaṃ rājan mahendrasyeva saṃyuge vimuñcantaṃ mahāstrāṇi pātayiṣyāmi taṃ rathāt
english: Behold my prowess in the fight, O king, as it were great Indra's: loosing mighty weapons, I will hurl him down from his car.

sanskrit: yaḥ śatruḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ macchatruḥ sa na saṃśayaḥ madarthā bhavadarthā ye ye madīyās tavaiva te
english: Whoever is an enemy of the sons of Pāṇḍu is my enemy too, beyond all doubt; my cause is yours, and those who are mine are yours alone.

sanskrit: tava bhrātā mama sakhā saṃbandhī śiṣya eva ca māṃsāny utkṛtya vai dadyām arjunārthe mahīpate
english: Your brother is my friend, my kinsman, and indeed my pupil; for Arjuna's sake, O lord of earth, I would cut off my own flesh and give it.

sanskrit: eṣa cāpi naravyāghro matkṛte jīvitaṃ tyajet eṣa naḥ samayas tāta tārayema parasparam sa māṃ niyuṅkṣva rājendra yāvad dvīpo bhavāmy aham
english: And this tiger among men would for my sake give up his life; this is our compact, dear one — that we should deliver each other across. So set me to the task, O lord of kings, that I may be your refuge.

sanskrit: pratijñātam upaplavye yat tat pārthena pūrvataḥ ghātayiṣyāmi gāṅgeyam ity ulūkasya saṃnidhau
english: That which was vowed before, at Upaplavya, by Pārtha in Ulūka's presence — 'I will bring about the death of the son of Gaṅgā' —

sanskrit: parirakṣyaṃ ca mama tad vacaḥ pārthasya dhīmataḥ anujñātaṃ tu pārthena mayā kāryaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: that word of the wise Pārtha I am bound to keep; and what Pārtha has consented to must be done by me, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: atha vā phalgunasyaiṣa bhāraḥ parimito raṇe nihaniṣyati saṃgrāme bhīṣmaṃ parapuraṃjayam
english: Or else this is a burden well within Phalguna's measure in battle: he will slay in the fray Bhīṣma, conqueror of hostile cities.

sanskrit: aśakyam api kuryād dhi raṇe pārthaḥ samudyataḥ tridaśān vā samudyuktān sahitān daityadānavaiḥ nihanyād arjunaḥ saṃkhye kim u bhīṣmaṃ narādhipa
english: For Pārtha, once roused, could accomplish even the impossible in battle: Arjuna might in combat slay the gods themselves, arrayed together with Daityas and Dānavas — how much more Bhīṣma, O lord of men!

sanskrit: viparīto mahāvīryo gatasattvo 'lpajīvitaḥ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo nūnaṃ kartavyaṃ nāvabudhyate
english: Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, mighty in valor, is surely now turned awry, his spirit gone, his life but short, and no longer perceives what ought to be done."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi mādhava sarve hy ete na paryāptās tava veganivāraṇe
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "So it is, O mighty-armed one, even as you say, O Mādhava; for none of these is a match to withstand your onset.

sanskrit: niyataṃ samavāpsyāmi sarvam eva yathepsitam yasya me puruṣavyāghra bhavān nātho mahābalaḥ
english: Assuredly I shall attain all that I desire, I for whom you, O tiger among men, mighty in strength, are protector.

sanskrit: sendrān api raṇe devāñ jayeyaṃ jayatāṃ vara tvayā nāthena govinda kim u bhīṣmaṃ mahāhave
english: With you as my protector, O best of the victorious, I could conquer in battle the very gods together with Indra, O Govinda — how much more Bhīṣma in the great fight!

sanskrit: na tu tvām anṛtaṃ kartum utsahe svārthagauravāt ayudhyamānaḥ sāhāyyaṃ yathoktaṃ kuru mādhava
english: Yet I will not, for the weight of my own interest, make your word a falsehood. Without yourself doing battle, render the aid that was promised, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: samayas tu kṛtaḥ kaś cid bhīṣmeṇa mama mādhava mantrayiṣye tavārthāya na tu yotsye kathaṃ cana duryodhanārthe yotsyāmi satyam etad iti prabho
english: A certain compact, O Mādhava, was made with me by Bhīṣma: 'I will counsel you for your good, but I will in no way fight for you; for Duryodhana's sake I shall fight' — truly this he said, O lord.

sanskrit: sa hi rājyasya me dātā mantrasyaiva ca mādhava tasmād devavrataṃ bhūyo vadhopāyārtham ātmanaḥ bhavatā sahitāḥ sarve pṛcchāmo madhusūdana
english: For he is the giver to me both of the kingdom and of counsel, O Mādhava. Therefore let us all, together with you, once more ask Devavrata himself the means of his own undoing, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: tad vayaṃ sahitā gatvā bhīṣmam āśu narottamam rucite tava vārṣṇeya mantraṃ pṛcchāma kauravam
english: So let us go together at once to Bhīṣma, that best of men, and — if it please you, O scion of Vṛṣṇi — ask the Kaurava for his counsel.

sanskrit: sa vakṣyati hitaṃ vākyaṃ tathyaṃ caiva janārdana yathā sa vakṣyate kṛṣṇa tathā kartāsmi saṃyuge
english: He will speak words salutary and true, O Janārdana; and as he shall direct, Kṛṣṇa, so shall I do in the battle.

sanskrit: sa no jayasya dātā ca mantrasya ca dhṛtavrataḥ bālāḥ pitrā vihīnāś ca tena saṃvardhitā vayam
english: He, firm in his vow, is the giver to us both of victory and of counsel; orphaned children bereft of our father, we were reared by him.

sanskrit: taṃ cet pitāmahaṃ vṛddhaṃ hantum icchāmi mādhava pituḥ pitaram iṣṭaṃ vai dhig astu kṣatrajīvikām
english: If I must wish to slay that aged grandsire, O Mādhava — my father's beloved father — then a curse upon the warrior's calling!"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato 'bravīn mahārāja vārṣṇeyaḥ kurunandanam rocate me mahābāho satataṃ tava bhāṣitam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O great king, the scion of Vṛṣṇi said to the delight of the Kurus: "Ever does your speech please me, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: devavrataḥ kṛtī bhīṣmaḥ prekṣitenāpi nirdahet gamyatāṃ sa vadhopāyaṃ praṣṭuṃ sāgaragāsutaḥ vaktum arhati satyaṃ sa tvayā pṛṣṭo viśeṣataḥ
english: Devavrata Bhīṣma, accomplished, could consume one with a mere glance. Let us go to ask the son of the ocean-bound river the means of his death; he is bound to tell the truth, especially when asked by you.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ tatra gacchāmaḥ praṣṭuṃ kurupitāmaham praṇamya śirasā cainaṃ mantraṃ pṛcchāma mādhava sa no dāsyati yaṃ mantraṃ tena yotsyāmahe parān
english: So let us go there to question the grandsire of the Kurus; bowing our heads to him, let us ask his counsel, O Mādhava. By the counsel he shall give us we will fight our foes."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃmantrya vai vīrāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ pāṇḍupūrvaja jagmus te sahitāḥ sarve vāsudevaś ca vīryavān vimuktaśastrakavacā bhīṣmasya sadanaṃ prati
english: Having thus taken counsel, the heroic Pāṇḍavas, O elder of Pāṇḍu, went all together, and the valiant Vāsudeva with them, their weapons and armor laid aside, to the tent of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: praviśya ca tadā bhīṣmaṃ śirobhiḥ pratipedire pūjayanto mahārāja pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabha praṇamya śirasā cainaṃ bhīṣmaṃ śaraṇam anvayuḥ
english: Entering then, the Pāṇḍavas approached Bhīṣma and saluted him with their heads, doing him honor, O great king, O bull of the Bhāratas; and bowing their heads to him, they took refuge with Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tān uvāca mahābāhur bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ svāgataṃ tava vārṣṇeya svāgataṃ te dhanaṃjaya svāgataṃ dharmaputrāya bhīmāya yamayos tathā
english: To them the mighty-armed Bhīṣma, grandsire of the Kurus, said: "Welcome to you, O scion of Vṛṣṇi; welcome to you, Dhanaṃjaya; welcome to the son of Dharma, to Bhīma, and to the twins as well.

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ vaḥ karomy adya yuṣmatprītivivardhanam sarvātmanā ca kartāsmi yady api syāt suduṣkaram
english: What service may I do you this day to increase your gladness? I will do it with my whole heart, even were it most hard to accomplish."

sanskrit: tathā bruvāṇaṃ gāṅgeyaṃ prītiyuktaṃ punaḥ punaḥ uvāca vākyaṃ dīnātmā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: To the son of Gaṅgā, who spoke thus again and again with affection, the son of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, sore at heart, said these words:

sanskrit: kathaṃ jayema dharmajña kathaṃ rājyaṃ labhemahi prajānāṃ saṃkṣayo na syāt kathaṃ tan me vadābhibho
english: "How may we conquer, O knower of dharma? How may we win the kingdom? How may there be no destruction of the people? Tell me that, O lord.

sanskrit: bhavān hi no vadhopāyaṃ bravītu svayam ātmanaḥ bhavantaṃ samare rājan viṣahema kathaṃ vayam
english: Tell us yourself the means of your own undoing; for how, O king, can we withstand you in battle?

sanskrit: na hi te sūkṣmam apy asti randhraṃ kurupitāmaha maṇḍalenaiva dhanuṣā sadā dṛśyo 'si saṃyuge
english: For there is in you not even the slightest gap, O grandsire of the Kurus; with your bow ever drawn into a full circle you are seen in the fight.

sanskrit: nādadānaṃ saṃdadhānaṃ vikarṣantaṃ dhanur na ca paśyāmas tvā mahābāho rathe sūryam iva sthitam
english: We cannot mark you taking up, nor nocking, nor drawing your bow, O mighty-armed one, stationed on your car like the sun.

sanskrit: narāśvarathanāgānāṃ hantāraṃ paravīrahan ka ivotsahate hantuṃ tvāṃ pumān bharatarṣabha
english: Slayer of men and horses, chariots and elephants, destroyer of hostile heroes — what man could presume to slay you, O bull of the Bhāratas?

sanskrit: varṣatā śaravarṣāṇi mahānti puruṣottama kṣayaṃ nītā hi pṛtanā bhavatā mahatī mama
english: By you, O best of men, pouring down your great showers of arrows, my mighty host has been brought to ruin.

sanskrit: yathā yudhi jayeyaṃ tvāṃ yathā rājyaṃ bhaven mama bhavet sainyasya vā śāntis tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: How I may conquer you in battle, how the kingdom may be mine, and how there may be peace for my army — tell me that, O grandsire."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīc chāṃtanavaḥ pāṇḍavān pāṇḍupūrvaja na kathaṃ cana kaunteya mayi jīvati saṃyuge yuṣmāsu dṛśyate vṛddhiḥ satyam etad bravīmi vaḥ
english: Then the son of Śaṃtanu said to the Pāṇḍavas, O elder of Pāṇḍu: "In no way, O son of Kuntī, while I live, will victory be seen for you in battle — this truth I tell you.

sanskrit: nirjite mayi yuddhe tu dhruvaṃ jeṣyatha kauravān kṣipraṃ mayi praharata yadīcchatha raṇe jayam anujānāmi vaḥ pārthāḥ praharadhvaṃ yathāsukham
english: But once I am overcome in the fight, you will surely conquer the Kauravas. Strike at me quickly, if you desire victory in battle; I grant you leave, O sons of Pṛthā — strike as you please.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi sukṛtaṃ manye bhavatāṃ vidito hy aham hate mayi hataṃ sarvaṃ tasmād evaṃ vidhīyatām
english: Thus indeed I deem it well done by you, for I am known to you; when I am slain, all is slain. Therefore let it be so ordained."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brūhi tasmād upāyaṃ no yathā yuddhe jayemahi bhavantaṃ samare kruddhaṃ daṇḍapāṇim ivāntakam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Tell us then the means by which we may conquer in battle you, who in your wrath are like Death himself, rod in hand.

sanskrit: śakyo vajradharo jetuṃ varuṇo 'tha yamas tathā na bhavān samare śakyaḥ sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
english: The wielder of the thunderbolt may be conquered, and Varuṇa, and Yama too; but you cannot be vanquished in battle even by gods and demons with Indra at their head."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca satyam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi pāṇḍava nāhaṃ śakyo raṇe jetuṃ sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: "True is this, O mighty-armed one, even as you say, O Pāṇḍava: I cannot be conquered in battle even by gods and demons with Indra at their head,

sanskrit: āttaśastro raṇe yatto gṛhītavarakārmukaḥ nyastaśastraṃ tu māṃ rājan hanyur yudhi mahārathāḥ
english: while in battle I stand armed and intent, my excellent bow in hand. But once I have laid down my weapons, O king, the great car-warriors may strike me in the fight.

sanskrit: nikṣiptaśastre patite vimuktakavacadhvaje dravamāṇe ca bhīte ca tavāsmīti ca vādini
english: Against one whose weapons are cast down, who has fallen, whose armor and banner are flung off, who is fleeing or afraid, or who says 'I am yours' —

sanskrit: striyāṃ strīnāmadheye ca vikale caikaputrake aprasūte ca duṣprekṣye na yuddhaṃ rocate mama
english: against a woman, or one bearing a woman's name, against the maimed, against one who is the only son, or unborn-of-issue, or unsightly — to fight with these pleases me not.

sanskrit: imaṃ ca śṛṇu me pārtha saṃkalpaṃ pūrvacintitam amaṅgalyadhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā na yudhyeyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: And hear this resolve of mine, O Pārtha, long ago conceived: beholding an inauspicious standard, I would in no way give battle.

sanskrit: ya eṣa draupado rājaṃs tava sainye mahārathaḥ śikhaṇḍī samarākāṅkṣī śūraś ca samitiṃjayaḥ
english: This son of Drupada in your host, O king, the great car-warrior Śikhaṇḍin, eager for battle, a hero victorious in assemblies of war —

sanskrit: yathābhavac ca strī pūrvaṃ paścāt puṃstvam upāgataḥ jānanti ca bhavanto 'pi sarvam etad yathātatham
english: how he was a woman before and afterward attained to manhood — you yourselves know all this exactly as it befell.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ samare śūraḥ puraskṛtya śikhaṇḍinam mām eva viśikhais tūrṇam abhidravatu daṃśitaḥ
english: Let the heroic Arjuna in battle, putting Śikhaṇḍin in the forefront, mailed and swift, rush upon me with his arrows.
